import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_bmi_processed.csv')
df.head()

# Filter the data to include only Hispanic men
hispanic_men = df[(df['GENDER'] == 'MALE') & (df['HISPANIC'] == 1)]

# Create a composite measure of time preference
# For simplicity, we will use DISSAVED as a proxy for time preference
# DISSAVED = 1 indicates that the respondent took more money out of than put into savings
# This could indicate a higher time preference for immediate rewards

# Perform a linear regression analysis to determine the relationship between time preference (DISSAVED) and BMI
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np

# Prepare the data for regression
X = hispanic_men[['DISSAVED']].values.reshape(-1, 1)  # Predictor (time preference)
y = hispanic_men['BMI'].values  # Response (BMI)

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficient
coefficient = model.coef_[0]
coefficient

# Get the p-value for the coefficient
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Prepare the data for regression with intercept
X = sm.add_constant(hispanic_men[['DISSAVED']])
y = hispanic_men['BMI']

# Create a linear regression model
model = sm.OLS(y, X).fit()

# Get the p-value for the coefficient
p_value = model.pvalues[1]
p_value
